questions.question: Describe the main parts of fair trade.
questions.expected_answer: Fair trade includes a fair minimum price that covers the cost of production even when world prices fall, an extra fair trade premium that producers decide together how to spend on community projects, standards for people such as no harmful child labour or forced labour, safe conditions and the right to join a union, and standards to protect the environment. Independent organisations check these standards and allow a fair trade label.

questions.question: Explain where rooibos grows and why small-scale farmers formed cooperatives.
questions.expected_answer: Rooibos grows naturally only in a small part of South Africa, mainly around the Cederberg and Clanwilliam and the nearby Bokkeveld. Small-scale farmers in poor rural communities had little land, money or access to markets, so they formed cooperatives, owned and run by their members, to process, pack and sell their tea together directly to fair trade buyers.

questions.question: Describe how fair trade has helped rooibos farmers and one limit of fair trade.
questions.expected_answer: Farmers receive fairer and more stable prices, a premium to spend on equipment, training and community needs, more control over their business and new skills, and they are encouraged to farm in ways that protect the environment. A limit is that fair trade products often cost more, so only some buyers choose them, and farmers still face problems like drought.
